answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The ripple multiplier is published, charged in sable, and ferrous lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3604 identities would post 3980 proofs and burn roughly 36 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
